newsitem.title: BOSNIA: OSCE cracks down on pre-election fraud in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: OSCE cracks down on pre-election fraud in Bosnia.

text.p: An international electoral commission announced penalties against Bosnian Serb and Croat authorities on Wednesday for intimidating voters and forging registration documents for upcoming local elections.
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) commission struck six candidates from municipal ballots in Serb-controlled territory and another candidate in a Croat-held town.
"People who are in control must understand after today's decision that they will be held accountable for their actions," OSCE spokesman David Foley told reporters.

The ruling, delivered by Norwegian Judge Finn Lynghjem, reflected a tougher approach by the OSCE towards fraud after national elections last year were plagued by allegations of abuses, OSCE officials said.

The commission concluded that the nationalist Serb Democratic Party (SDS), which rules Bosnia's Serb entity, tried to falsify registration forms and coerced voters to register in certain areas by threatening to withhold humanitarian aid.
The SDS behaved similarly before the 1996 vote.

The more recent evidence of fraudulent registration documents indicated that Serb authorities sought "to circumvent the registration rules in order to consolidate their power" in municipal elections scheduled for September, the commission said.
The OSCE disqualified the SDS from standing in elections in the village of Srpski Drvar, where more than half of the 50 registration forms showed signs of tampering and fraud.
The election appeals subcommission also sacked four officials running voter registration centres because they had threatened OSCE supervisors and interpreters or orchestrated fraud.
In the western town of Drvar, nationalist Croat authorities were punished for discouraging Serb refugees from returning to their pre-war homes.
The OSCE accused the Croats of flouting electoral rules which call for voting to be held in an atmosphere free of fear and intimidation.

The ruling party in Drvar, the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ), tolerated the destruction of houses formerly inhabited by Serbs and helped organise mobs to block buses of refugees trying to visit the area, the commission said.

Officials of the HDZ, which is the Bosnian wing of the governing party in neighbouring Croatia, were also forcing voters to submit registration forms or attend political rallies to obtain humanitarian aid.
The OSCE threatened to disquality more HDZ candidates if authorities failed to halt politically motivated violence or intimidation.
Bosnia's first municipal elections since the 1992-95 war were supposed to coincide with parliamentary elections held last September.
The OSCE mission postponed the municipal vote because of irregularities in the voter registration process, pinning most of the blame again on the Serbs.
